name: Move deals along the pipeline from what actually happened
summary: Moves open deals along the pipeline from what actually happened, not from what someone meant to do. A daily scan reads the open deals and drafts a register of deals with no recorded change for the set number of days. Each stage move, recorded from the deal's notes and activity, is queued for approval, and a person approves it before the CRM changes. Nothing moves in the CRM until a person approves it.

covered_by.signal-received: agent judgment on the deal's notes and activity (see SKILL.md); the scan records each deal's last change
covered_by.decide-move: agent judgment, recorded as a move; queue turns it into an approval
covered_by.update-stage: queued stage change, approved by a person
covered_by.set-next-action: not built (task creation is not a mapped draft operation)
covered_by.stale-deal-review: scan (register of open deals with no change for the set number of days)
covered_by.close-won-or-lost: person (won or lost stays with the owner)
covered_by.record-keeping: register and moves in the workflow store; approval history in the CRM shell

crons.name: scan
crons.summary: Daily (20:00 UTC, 6 or 7 am in eastern Australia): reads the open deals in the pipeline and drafts a register of deals with no recorded change for the set number of days. Changes nothing in the CRM.

crons.name: queue
crons.summary: Daily (21:00 UTC): re-reads each pending stage move, checks it still goes forward along the pipeline, and queues it for approval. A stage change runs only when a person approves it.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations here are reads only. The register and the moves live in the workflow store, so a scan writes nothing to the CRM. A stage change moves a live deal, so it is a live operation that waits for a person.

gohighlevel.covers: open opportunities in one pipeline: the stalled register, and stage moves queued for approval

pipedrive.covers: open deals in one pipeline: the stalled register, and stage moves queued for approval

gaps: Nothing records a stage-move decision yet. The workflow CLI's propose command only takes quote lines, and core/ is not changed by this build. Until a decide command or a CRM shell form writes the moves store, the queue cron has nothing to queue.

The judgment that moves a deal is an agent step in SKILL.md. No mapped operation reads call transcripts or emails tied to a deal on either platform, so the agent reads them by hand or through the CRM.
Zoho CRM: its deal endpoints are not mapped (only link-email operations are), so there is no adapter.
Stage gates (for example a deposit paid before the job starts) are not built. The platforms' If/Else steps cannot express a required field that blocks a stage change.
Set next action (creating a task or activity) is not built: task creation is not a mapped draft operation on GoHighLevel, and Pipedrive activity creation is not wired here.
Hand-to-delivery (turning a won deal into a job or roster) is not built; it belongs to the fulfilment platform.
Pipedrive's last change is the deal's update or stage-change time. An unrelated field edit counts as a change, so a stalled deal can look fresh.
GoHighLevel's last action date is the platform's own field. Whether it moves on every call or email needs a check on a real account.
The stage order is typed in settings. Pipedrive's stage list (order_nr) is mapped but not read, so a reorder in the CRM is not picked up.
Both adapters are offline-tested only, with a fake network. Neither is proven against a real account.
